04-213.r: Long-term agricultural credit → Land Development Banks (earlier called Land Mortgage Banks).

04-214.r: Largest source of farm credit → Commercial Banks (about three-fourth; 53.7% in 1999-2000 → 76.86% in 2022-23); co-operatives fell from 39.5% to 10.80%.

04-217.r: Least institutional credit to agriculture → Foreign Private Banks (negligible); main sources are Commercial, Cooperative and Regional Rural Banks.

04-218.r: Agricultural credit target: 2020-21 → Rs. 15 lakh crore; 2021-22 → 16.5; 2022-23 → 18; 2023-24 → 20 lakh crore.

04-219.r: Kisan Credit Card (1998; NABARD model, R.V. Gupta Committee) → short-term credit for farm-asset working capital, household consumption, post-harvest expenses; not tractors, houses, cold storage.

04-223.r: Chronology → Regional Rural Banks (1975), NABARD (1982), SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (1992-93), Kisan Credit Card (1998).

04-224.r: UPA's New Package for Agriculture → bank loans to landless farmers, NABARD proposal for them, credit to 50 lakh new farmers; no loan waiver or repayment concession.

04-225.r: Price Stabilisation Fund Scheme (1 April 2003 – 30 September 2013) → small coffee, tea, rubber, tobacco growers (up to four hectares); book answer: potato and onion.
04-225.c: Explanation says the PSF of that period covered coffee, tea, rubber, tobacco, which fits (c); printed (a) potato and onion fits only the later PSF.

04-226.r: Price Stabilization Fund (2014-15) → curbs price volatility of onions and potatoes (pulses added later) through a strategic buffer; discourages hoarding.

04-227.r: Sand → 'minor mineral' under MMDR Act, 1957 (true); States grant minor mineral leases and also frame their rules, not the Centre → 1 and 3 correct.

05-001.r: First Indian private company in Fortune Global 500 → Reliance Industries (284th, list of 24 July 2006); 2023: Reliance 88th, Indian Oil 94th, LIC 107th.

05-002.r: Biggest company in Fortune India 500 list (2019 to 2023) → Reliance Industries; 2023: Indian Oil 2nd, LIC 3rd.

05-003.r: PNGRB (2006) → not India's first regulator (Forward Market Commission 1952, SEBI, IRDA earlier); ensures competitive gas markets; appeals go to Appellate Tribunal for Electricity.

05-004.r: CSR made mandatory from April 1, 2014 (India first in world) by Section 135, Companies Act 2013 → two percent of average net profit of past three years.
05-004.t: Both statements wrong: the Act is of 2013 (not 2014) and the spend is two percent (not one).

05-006.r: Uday Kotak Committee (SEBI, June 2017) → corporate governance: at least half board independent, minimum 6 members, one woman independent director; chairman and MD posts not same.

05-007.r: Indian Railways targets → 100% electrification by 2023 (about 95% broad gauge done by FY 2023-24) and 'net zero' carbon emission network by 2030 (both correct).

05-008.r: India's first rubber-tyred Metro → Nashik, Maharashtra (cleared by State Cabinet, August 2019); rubber tyres run on concrete or steel rollways.

05-009.r: IKEA's first showroom in India → Hyderabad, 9 August 2018 (13 acres, about 7500 products).

05-010.r: Industrial Development Centre Banmore → Morena district, Madhya Pradesh.

05-011.r: Madhya Pradesh 'towns of export excellence' → Dewas (pharmaceuticals) and Indore (soya meal and soya products).

05-012.r: Committee on revisiting and revitalising PPP model of infrastructure → Dr. Vijay Kelkar (announced in Budget 2015-16; report 19 November 2015).

05-013.r: Bharatmala Project → road and highways infrastructure (economic corridors, inter corridors, feeder routes).

05-014.r: National Infrastructure Pipeline → first made public in PM's 2019 Independence Day speech; aims at equitable infrastructure access (R true); '2020-30 period' is false (A false).

05-015.r: PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan → launched 13 October 2021 (not 2022); seven engines: roads, railways, airports, ports, mass transport, waterways, logistics; NIP aligned to it.

05-016.r: Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor → developed with Japan (MoU 2006); Japan also assists Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.

05-017.r: Deepak Parekh Committee (Finance Ministry, December 26, 2006) → financing infrastructure development; report May 2007; headed infrastructure financing committee again July 2012.

05-018.r: India → second largest mobile phone producer after China (ICA data, 2017); retained in 2023-24.

05-019.r: National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (2015) → India's first infrastructure-specific fund; not a NITI Aayog organ; proposed corpus Rs. 40,000 crore, not Rs. 4,00,000 crore.

05-020.r: PLI for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing (notified 1 April 2020) → boosts mobile phone and specified component manufacturing (incl. ATMP units); 4% to 6% incentive on incremental sales.

05-021.r: National Manufacturing Policy → 4 November 2011; manufacturing to 25% of GDP within a decade, 100 million jobs, 12-14% sector growth.

05-024.r: NMP initiatives for manufacturing → National Investment and Manufacturing Zones, single window clearance, Technology Acquisition and Development Fund (all three).

05-025.r: First National Investment and Manufacturing Zone proposed → Prakasam district, Andhra Pradesh; NIMZs are tools of National Manufacturing Policy, 2011.

05-026.r: Make in India (25 September 2014) → facilitate investment, innovation, skills, IP protection, best manufacturing infrastructure; aims cover more than one option.

05-028.r: Make in India logo → silhouette of a lion on the move; initiative launched September 2014.

05-030.r: Not an industrial development initiative → Digital India (digitally empowered society, knowledge economy); Make in India, Ease of Doing Business, Start-up India are.

05-031.r: Start-up funding → bootstrapping, crowd funding, angel investors, venture capital, incubators, bank loans, MUDRA (all the above).

05-032.r: 'New age financing can meet start-up needs' (angel investors, venture capital, crowd funding) → President Pranab Mukherjee, 17th March 2016.

05-033.r: Student Startup and Innovation Policy (SSIP) 2.0 → Gujarat, January 2022 (for 11 January 2022 to 31 March 2027).

05-034.r: Stand-Up India → promotes entrepreneurship among SC/ST and women; refinance through SIDBI; anchored by Department of Financial Services (both true).

05-035.r: Stand-Up India (5 April 2016) → bank loans of 10 lakh to 1 crore to at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower per branch for a greenfield enterprise.

05-037.r: PM MUDRA Yojana (April 8, 2015) → brings small entrepreneurs into formal finance; loans up to 10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm micro enterprises.

05-039.r: MUDRA loan types → Shishu up to Rs. 50,000; Kishor more than Rs. 50,000 up to Rs. 5,00,000.
05-039.h: Shishu (child) gets the smallest loan; Kishor (teen) the next size.

05-040.r: Quality Council of India (1997) → set up jointly by Government and Indian industry; chairman appointed by PM on industry's recommendation (both true); under DPIIT.

05-041.r: Chronology → Minimum Wages Act (1948), Industries (Development and Regulation) Act (1951), MRTP Act (1969), FERA (1973).

05-042.r: Post-1991 reforms and dilution of MRTP Act provisions → mergers and acquisitions became common → A and R true, R explains A.

05-043.r: Data on industrial disputes, closures, retrenchments, lay-offs → Labour Bureau (established 1920).

05-044.r: Trade Disputes Act 1929 → Courts of Inquiry and Boards of Conciliation; banned strikes/lock-outs without notice in public utility services.

05-045.r: Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Central (Amendment) Rules 2018 → fixed-term employment eases lay-offs; no termination notice for temporary workmen (both true).

05-046.r: Factories Act 1881 → better working conditions (no child labour under seven); did not fix wages or allow trade unions; N.M. Lokhande → pioneer of labour movement.

05-047.r: Code on Wages 2019 replaced → Payment of Wages Act 1936, Minimum Wages Act 1948, Payment of Bonus Act 1965, Equal Remuneration Act 1976; not Contract Labour Act.

05-048.r: Casual workers → entitled to EPF (Supreme Court, Pawan Hans case, January 2020), regular hours and overtime; government can mandate wages only by bank account (all three).

05-049.r: UP minimum wage for unskilled labour from 1 April 2017 → Rs. 7400 per month; from 1 April 2024 → Rs. 10648.

05-050.r: Industry's share in GDP 2006-07 → 25-30%; was 16.6% in 1950-51; averaged 31 percent during 2011-12 to 2020-21.

05-052.r: 1999-2000: industrial production rose, helped by stable exchange rate and better business sentiment after South-East Asian crisis → A, R true; R explains A.

05-053.r: IIP (by NSO, monthly) covers mining, manufacturing, electricity; construction is not included (nor gas and water supply).
hi: Index of Industrial Production (औद्योगिक उत्पादन सूचकांक)

05-055.r: Index of Industrial Production → earlier released by CSO, now by National Statistical Office (NSO), monthly; base year 2011-12.

05-056.r: IIP base year 1993-94 → 2004-05 (10th June 2011) → 2011-12 (May 12, 2017); weights: manufacturing 77.63%, mining 14.37%, electricity 7.99%.

05-057.r: Eight core industries → coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilizers, steel, cement, electricity (not textiles or chemicals); 40.27% of IIP weight (earlier 37.90%).

05-059.r: Highest weight in Index of Eight Core Industries → electricity generation; eight core industries = 40.27 percent of IIP weight (base 2011-12).

05-060.r: Highest growth in 2000-01 among options → steel; in 2023-24 steel (12.3%) again led cement, coal and electricity.

05-061.r: Coal nationalised by Indira Gandhi government (Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973) (true); coal blocks now auctioned, not by lottery (Act of 2015); self-sufficiency claim false.
